results.message: How did someone become a Christian in your church?

voice_event.speaker: lpc
voice_event.text: You were taught before you were washed. We told you what you were joining before you joined it. You said the creed back, and then we baptized you. That teaching took time, and it was not a formality. Augustine wrote a whole guide on how to do it, for a deacon who had asked him. You learned it by heart before the water, not after. After the baptism, you came to the table. The same bread, the same cup, was set before whoever had walked the road to it. And the bishop who baptized you answered for you. That charge ran both ways. He preached to you and taught you, and when you failed it was not a problem he managed but a wound he carried. You could stand in front of his seat and refuse to leave until he heard you. If you did fail, there was a road back, and it was walked where everyone could see it. Your name was set down first. What had truly changed in you was watched and weighed by someone answerable for weighing it rightly. Augustine says to correct with words, or blows if need be, yet forgive in the heart, as a surgeon cuts from kindness: “Let us rebuke with words, and with blows if need be. But let us also forgive the sin and cast the fault out of our hearts. The Lord added “from your hearts” for this reason: when discipline is given out of love, gentleness must not leave the heart. For what is as kind and gentle as a surgeon with his knife?”
